verdict:
The fixes for gbf-dev-09 hold. gbf-dev-07 and gbf-test-16 each still have one medium problem: a shortcut answer passes V5 and the review records do not report it.

Gates: I re-ran `./gb tier-f gates` on byte-identical copies in ~/grc-bench-work/review/g10r/copy/. All five gates pass for all three tasks, and each gates.json matches the committed one:
- dev-07: solvability 10/10, 578 tokens, 8/8 variants, start fails at V5 (f2p false, p2p true), 13/13 mutants killed.
- dev-09: 10/10, 968 tokens, 15/15 variants, start fails at V5 (f2p false, p2p true), 26/26 killed.
- test-16: 10/10, 775 tokens, 21/21 variants, start fails at V5 (f2p false, p2p true), 15/15 killed.

Rebuild: each build.py, run from a scratch tree (~/grc-bench-work/review/g10r/regen), regenerates task.json, start.grc, reference.grc and every variant byte-identically. Their seed-split and sha256 asserts pass: dev-07 and dev-09 use dev seeds, test-16 a test seed.

Accepted fixes I confirmed:
- dev-07: the whole-capture exact check (8190 samples, max_offset 0), the Throttle graph check, the run sentence and the observation types.
- dev-09: value_only plus isomorphic connection checks, the rewritten v2/v3 that obey the scope sentence, the start-graph rrc.dat corr_ref plus RMS checks, and the slice-rule wording. A further valid answer also passes V5: swap the lp/hp taps' variable references, then set the variables by meaning (d9_q2_valid_swapped_refs).
- test-16: the absolute tone frequencies, the 4th tone and the ch2 rate check, the noise-share check (30 %), the achievable filter wording, the run sentence, and the FFT-based variants (they no longer hit the old tap stall).

Rejections:
- dev-07 'compliance:F3 as a gate mutant' is justified. gates.py applies exactly one edit.py operator per mutant, and no single set_param, rewire_input, bypass or set_id makes the Stream Mux emit the header after the frame.
- test-16 'item-quality:F4' is properly left to the team.

Not reported because they are low severity: dev-09 still passes V5 with samp_rate 96000 and every cutoff and width doubled (d9_q1). So the claim in spec_properties that the band checks catch a sample-rate change does not hold for an exactly compensated change. No task was re-themed.

Probes are in ~/grc-bench-work/review/g10r/probes/. The scripts are g10r_probes.py and g10r_t16_noisefloor.py in the session scratchpad, with copies in ~/grc-bench-work/review/g10r/.

findings.claim: The fix for compliance:F2 / item-quality:F2 does not enforce the stated requirement 'The frames must still be built from streams A and B by multiplexing (I will change the streams later)'. The p2p path check passes as soon as any one Vector Source reaches any File Sink through any block in MERGERS. Two shortcuts therefore pass: (a) multiplexing only stream B with a hand-made copy of stream A that already contains the headers; (b) the round-1 hard-coded shortcut, unchanged except that it is fed through the existing Stream Mux set to one input. The records understate this hole. The resolution says 'The hard-coded 18-value shortcut now fails'. review.notes (1) says only a 'deliberately disguised fixed output routed through a merging block (e.g. an Add with a zero source)' would pass.
findings.evidence: Both probes were run with ladder.check and the task loaded through taskio.load. (1) ~/grc-bench-work/review/g10r/probes/d7_p1_doctored_copy_of_A.grc is the start graph plus a Vector Source (-1, -2, 1, 2, 3, 4, -1, -2, 8, 9, 10, 11) on Stream Mux input 0 in place of stream A, with lengths [6, 3]; stream A now feeds only stream_a.dat. Result: highest V5, first_failed null, groups f2p true / p2p true, no graph-check failures. Stream A no longer reaches mux_out.dat, so the user's announced later change of stream A would have no effect. (2) d7_p2_hardcoded_via_1in_mux.grc is the start graph with the Stream Mux set to num_inputs 1, lengths [18], fed by one Vector Source holding the 18 output values. Result: V5 pass, all checks and graph checks true. Both answers take one change_graph edit.
findings.suggested_fix: Preferred: a tooling feature that anchors the structural check on what feeds the observation points, so the check is name-independent. For example, 'the block feeding stream_a.dat (and likewise stream_b.dat) reaches the File Sink mux_out.dat', or a path check with from_params on the Vector Source's vector. Until then, rewrite review.notes (1) to state the real limit: any single Vector Source through any merging block satisfies the check, including a header-baked copy of one stream multiplexed with the other, and the round-1 shortcut routed through the existing Stream Mux with one input. Also correct the resolution's 'now fails' claim, so the team's keep-or-drop decision on this sentence rests on accurate information.

findings.claim: Nothing ties ch0.dat-ch3.dat to the summed input. The task has no graph_checks, and every channel check reads only the tone's offset and RMS. So an answer that writes synthetic tones (Signal Sources at 12 kHz with the stated offsets and amplitudes) to the channel files passes V5 without any channelizing. This is the 'answer that writes the expected output' shortcut. It breaks the stated requirement to channelize the sum ('Change the channel plan to four channels ... signals 10 kHz or more from it must be filtered out ... plus a little noise'). review.notes does not record it, contrary to R4 / R9 / R11 of the fix plan. A cheap signal check that every valid design passes closes it.
findings.evidence: ~/grc-bench-work/review/g10r/probes/t16_s1_hardcoded_channels.grc is the start graph with the channelizer deleted, a new complex ch3.dat sink, and four analog_sig_source_x (samp_rate 12000; 1200 Hz / 0.8, 1920 Hz / 0.5, -960 Hz / 0.2, -1440 Hz / 0.3) wired straight to ch0-ch3. Result: highest V5, first_failed null, f2p and p2p true. t16_s2_hardcoded_3_channels.grc (the reference channelizer kept for ch0 only, ch1-ch3 synthetic) also passes V5. I added probe checks: band_fraction, Hann window, fs 12000, skip 1024, n 3072, on a 1.8 kHz tone-free sub-band within 2 kHz of each centre ([-2000, -200] Hz for ch0 and ch1, [200, 2000] Hz for ch2 and ch3). The reference gives 2.3e-5 / 5.5e-5 / 3.48e-4 / 1.82e-4. All 21 variants stay within about -10 % to +20 % of those values: ch0 2.3e-5, ch1 5.5e-5 to 6.5e-5, ch2 3.47e-4 to 3.75e-4, ch3 1.71e-4 to 1.82e-4. S1 gives 0 / 0 / 0 / 0, and S2 gives 2.3e-5 / 0 / 0 / 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an f2p noise-floor check on each channel. Derive the threshold from the stated noise amplitude 0.02, for example min = 0.5 x the expected share in such a sub-band. State it in the instruction, e.g. 'the input noise near each channel centre must come through at its original level'. Put the synthetic-tone probe into build.py --probes, and add a gate mutant that the check alone kills. Alternatively, or as well, record the limit in review.notes for the team. Note that a graph check such as 'a path from the Add through a channel-selection block to a File Sink' would still accept S2.
